manuscript_references.text: Supplementary Section S13 records the primary-source versions and actual reading scopes for these comparisons. The targeted search establishes neither global priority nor a complete equation-by-equation audit of the predecessors.

Policies within 10⁻⁶ score units of the saved primary EV optimum are retained. The range describes policy ambiguity, not a statistical interval. Section 5.3 reports the A/B baseline comparison and Supplementary Section S2 supplies bounds, full policy sets and fixed-policy differences.

The frozen 23-event optimization suite contains 555 configurations: two baselines; 21 readiness-budget or resource conditions for each of the legacy and inventory models; 26 spatial conditions; eight intervention subsets; 56 one-factor perturbations; 400 paired joint-perturbation configurations; nine procurement limits; five existing-stock conditions; five price conditions; and two restricted-access conditions. The legacy model omits explicit pump procurement, stock and access. Its comparison with the inventory model is a bundled specification comparison, separated from the controlled components below. Supplementary Sections S1.1 and S5–S9 retain grid definitions, full procurement ranges and noncore results, including the correction that recomputes linking bounds when primitive resource data change.

The retained optimization runs use Python 3.12.8 and Gurobi 13.0.2, one thread, seed 0, zero relative and absolute MIP-gap targets, feasibility/integrality tolerances of 10⁻⁸ and a 60-second per-solve limit. Saved objectives, feasibility and information-value ordering were reconstructed, with independent HiGHS RP checks. Supplementary Sections S1 and S13.1 distinguish the historical designs and verification from the later targeted A/B, component and coverage validation. This v3 integration reuses those completed analyses; it adds no optimization runs or stress tests.

Completed component comparisons hold all benefits, readiness costs, operating resources and integer deployments fixed within each frequency/capital panel. F0 removes the inventory row while retaining capital and continuous procurement; F1 applies the entire stock separately in each sector, a deliberately replicated-stock counterfactual; F2 replaces those rows with a shared total; and F3 additionally requires integer procurement. Access branches allow pumping only in Tai O1 or only in Tai O2. The two capital panels are HKD 2 million and a separately specified hypothetical HKD 6.5 million, with N0 = 0 and HKD 1 million per pump. Only RP is evaluated for these 24 specifications. Supplementary Section S3 gives all results and a feasible-set witness.

The original historically selected sample contains 23 named tropical-cyclone-related records. Their annual counts are 5, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3 and 3 for 2017–2025. Computational cleaning finds unique nonblank identifiers and finite indicators for all 23, with no imputation or cleaning-stage exclusions. Rainfall stations are R11 for 19 events, HKA for three and R12 for one [18]. Supplementary Section S10 preserves these vectors and original anchors. The new fixed station hierarchy is compatible with these four non-R11 choices, but compatibility does not recover their historical reasons.

The separately reconstructed local-warning frame contains 203 warning segments in 62 warning groups, cross-checked against annual local-warning tables for 2017–2024 and the full twelve official monthly summaries for 2025 [21]. Resolving repeated passages and the two depressions sharing a 2021 warning gives 63 cyclone identities [23,26]. All 22 cyclones with highest local signal at least 8 are present in the old sample, along with Signal-1 Man-yi. This is a retrospective description, not proof that an “at least 8 plus exception” rule was historically used. Supplementary Section S12 reports the annual candidate and analyzability counts.

The preceding source audit recovered complete official tables for all 23 frozen W/S pairs, including Pakhar, Toraji, Wipha 2025, Tapah and Ragasa; Supplementary Section S10 retains registered links and verified alternatives [19]. The subsequent CI-01 comparison adds official database evidence and preserves the Yagi date conflict rather than treating every time field as verified. It retains 48 complete 2017–2024 tide tables, 14 target 2025 monthly-report tables and the relevant complete PDF snapshots, target-page images, retrieval records and hashes. These materials support source traceability, not independent instrument calibration. The historical candidate/exclusion register, original anchor definitions and contemporaneous station-substitution decisions remain unrecovered.

The original readiness budget is 20,000 CU. Each scenario has 30,000 CU of operating budget and abstract capacities of 400 labour units, 60 equipment units and 220 supply units. Sector-specific costs and resource requirements are equal in the baseline. The sector benefit modifiers are β1 = 1.1 and β2 = 0.9. Table 5 gives the component scores and readiness amounts, while Supplementary Section S11 lists the scenario-dependent requirements.

Source: completed supplementary validation, ev_summary.csv and ev_optimal_policies.csv (Supplementary Section S2). The new 60-frequency mobile baseline selects one new pump; two-pump EV optima have higher EEV = 626.497667. The corresponding RP and WS are reported in Table 14.

Figure 2 retains the frozen 23-event procurement results under A. RP remains 616.082500 at limits zero, one and two, changes to a pumping policy at three, and reaches 686.007826 at the tested six-pump limit. At several higher limits the full EV-optimal policy range includes zero VSS, despite a positive value for the minimum-procurement returned policy. Supplementary Section S9 gives complete 23- and 60-frequency procurement tables; these thresholds are hypothetical model results.

The sets differ despite zero F1-to-F2 objective change. With two purchased pumps and Drainage readiness in both sectors, assigning two pumps to each sector satisfies the replicated rows and all primitive resources but violates shared stock (four assignments exceed two pumps). Supplementary Section S3 verifies this witness and reports all 24 component/access specifications, including the hypothetical HKD 6.5 million panel. At that larger envelope, limiting pump access to Tai O2 lowers RP by 53.259130 and 60.965167 respectively; the zero access effect at the no-pump baseline is therefore instance-specific.

Procurement integrality alone has zero RP effect for a structural reason. For any feasible continuous n, integer deployment requires an integer maximum simultaneous pump demand across scenarios. Replacing n with that demand minus integer initial stock, truncated below at zero, gives an integer procurement no larger than n, with unchanged readiness, deployment and score. Capital use cannot increase. F2 and F3 consequently have identical projected (y, x) feasible sets in the present formulation. This proof depends on procurement entering only the capital cap, stock row and secondary choice rule; it does not cover altered purchasing relations or fractional deployment (Supplementary Section S3).

For k = 1 or 2, the returned optimal policy prepares Barrier and Warning in Tai O1 and Warning in Tai O2 for 18,500 CU, with no new pumps. It moves k Warning packages from Tai O1 to Tai O2 in each scenario. No uniqueness of deployment is claimed. The k = 6 control requires at least twelve units in Extreme, each requiring at least 42 labour units: 504 exceeds the capacity of 400 even before other constraints. Its infeasibility is retained, not converted into a zero score. Only RP has been evaluated for these altered feasible sets; Supplementary Section S4 supplies deployment and certificates.

The frozen spatial grid, intervention-subset ablation, one-factor perturbations, joint hypothetical draws and legacy bound-correction results are retained in Supplementary Sections S5–S8. They document dependence on assumptions, rather than additional field validation.

The existing ten-case reconstructed-frequency EV audit enumerates 1,716 feasible first-stage policies and records 1,808 additional audit solves. Its two-pump baseline has four EV optima, whereas several limits of at least six admit zero VSS. These broader procurement ranges use A only (Supplementary Section S9). The newer targeted A/B, component and coverage package comprises 500 main solves (498 OPTIMAL and two intentionally INFEASIBLE) and 936 independent HiGHS optimizations. Its maximum primary-objective difference is 1.3074 × 10⁻¹¹. These are results of the completed review package, not experiments added during v3 preparation; their agreement supports numerical implementation within the stated scope, not journal acceptability or empirical validity.

Likewise, Warning's largest Shapley contribution in the frozen subset analysis describes its role under the chosen additive value function (Supplementary Section S6). It does not identify a causal ranking of real warning, barrier and pumping programmes. Hydraulic interactions, repeated protection of the same assets, warning uptake, saturation and spatial exposure remain outside the response scores. Independent optima across hypothetical parameter draws do not define a single robust policy.

Data and code availability. The project retains the frozen master workbook, original 23-event inputs and model, result workbooks, 555 configuration solutions, census geometry and seven manuscript figures. The separate CI-01 package retains the screening protocol and amendments; candidate, audit and reconciliation CSVs; official-source manifests and snapshots; final 60-event inputs; common-59 station data; scenario and migration results; the 555-case frequency-only replay and repeat; and EV-policy audit logs. Supplementary Sections S10 and S12 retain the original event-source ledger and reconstructed candidate flow. The completed targeted review package additionally retains EV A/B enumeration, component/coverage models, saved solutions and independent checks. Versioned audit records preserve file hashes, source access scopes and manuscript consistency checks. Final_Submission_Readiness.md and Remaining_Submission_Blockers.md distinguish submission actions from disclosed scientific limitations. TODO-A6: specify the public repository or archival DOI, version and access conditions for the submission package. No public deposit is asserted here.

[18] Hong Kong Observatory. (n.d.). Daily meteorological records at Ngong Ping Fresh Water Reservoir (R11), Hong Kong International Airport (HKA), and Discovery Bay (R12), 2017–2025. Station-year source links are listed in Supplementary Section S10. Source.

[19] Hong Kong Observatory. (n.d.). Tropical cyclone reports and event tables of maximum sea level and maximum storm surge, 2017–2025. Event-specific source links and verification limits are listed in Supplementary Section S10. Official event tables corroborate the frozen 23 numerical W/S pairs; E020 is a joint northeast-monsoon and Man-yi rise. The subsequent database cross-check leaves Yagi's surge-peak date unresolved. Recovered table locators and source alternatives are described in Section 4.3 and Supplementary Section S10. Source.

Supplementary_Methods_and_Results.md accompanies this candidate. Sections S1–S4 provide verification scope, EV A/B detail, controlled components and hypothetical coverage; S5–S9 retain noncore and procurement results; S10–S12 retain original event sources, scenario requirements and candidate flow; and S13 records source-reading limits. Main-text Figures 1 and 2 and supplementary figures retain the frozen image files.
